title: or
goal: This lesson covers how or is True when at least one side is True.
learn: Know that one True side is enough
idea: The keyword or joins two conditions. The whole thing is True if at least one side is True, so the only way to get False is False or False. Use it when either option is enough, like having a coupon or a member pass.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change is_member = True to is_member = False and press Run. You should see Full price.

practice.text: Set raining and snowing. Make raining True and snowing False. If either is True, print Stay inside.
practice.hint: or is True when at least one side is True. Raining is already True, so you only need one if that checks both weather flags.
practice.starterTip: Try if raining or snowing: then indented below: print("Stay inside").
practice.starter:
raining = True
snowing = False
# if with or
practice.gradingNote: Pass if or is used and Stay inside prints.

practice.hint: One side of or can be False as long as the other side is True. Wrap the whole expression in print().
practice.starterTip: Try print((3 == 4) or (3 < 5)). The first part is False but the second is True, so the result is True.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if output is True using or.

quiz.question: When is A or B True?

options.text: When at least one is True

quiz.correct: Right, one True side is enough for or.
quiz.wrong: or only fails when both sides are False.

quiz.question: What is False or False?
quiz.correct: Yes, with no True side the answer is False.
quiz.wrong: or needs at least one True side.

quiz.question: How is or different from and?

options.text: or needs one True; and needs both True

quiz.correct: Right, or needs one True and and needs both.
quiz.wrong: Remember that and is stricter than or.
